text:
Marta (Support): heads up - customer Ingrid from AcmeReports is seeing intermittent failures and big tail spikes on the embeddings endpoint. started at ~13:02 UTC, persists across regions. error shows 'vector length mismatch' sometimes and otherwise timeouts. can we triage? :eyes:
Ingrid (Customer): yes, we started seeing it after a deploy this morning. some requests get a dimension error, others succeed but with 400-700ms latency. it's flaky. we've pinned an example conversation and request ids if that helps.
Marta (Support): thanks. can you paste one failing request + response?
Ingrid (Customer): sample: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-large","input": ["foo"]}'
Response: {"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536"} (request_id: req_9a3b)
Ingrid (Customer): other times it returns a 200 with a 1536-d vector. we didn't change the client.
Marta (Support): good repro. I'm opening a ticket and tagging eng-runtime + SRE. support-bot: created SUP-6712 for Ingrid.
support-bot: Ticket SUP-6712 created and linked to this thread.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): ping, thanks for the details. quick hypothesis: we onboarded a newer embedding variant (rwd-embed-large-v2) that defaults to 1536 dims but our routing rules might still advertise 1024 for some customer pins. two paths: either the routing picks the wrong model variant, or batching merges requests across model variants and returns the wrong vector.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): can you share the customer's model pinning config?
Marta (Support): Ingrid says they never pinned explicitly; they call model "rwd-embed-large" and expect 1024 like before.
Devon (SRE): I'll pull runtime histograms. which endpoints / route? support, can you give me request ids and approx times?
Ingrid (Customer): we have a small log dump: req_9a3b (13:02:14), req_9a4c (13:02:17), req_9b01 (13:04:03). some are OK, some fail.
Devon (SRE): grabbing batch_size histograms from the region - I see spikes where batch sizes jump to ~128 even though max_batch_size config is 64 for that pool. also see increased tail latency in the embedding worker queue.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): interesting. our dynamic batcher has two knobs: max_batch_size (per-queue cap) and cross_variant_coalesce (allows different variants to be batched together if compatible). if a newer variant landed on some nodes with a different dim it can lead to mixed replies. are we allowed to coalesce variants for embeds? we generally shouldn't if dims differ.
Marta (Support): customer is not using variant mixing intentionally.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): can you paste the runtime config from that pool?
Devon (SRE): config snapshot: ```
pool: embeddings-east-1
dynamic_batching: true
max_batch_size: 64
batch_window_ms: 12
cross_variant_coalesce: true
shard_count: 4
```
Devon (SRE): note cross_variant_coalesce true. that could explain how a 1024 request gets bundled with a 1536 worker and then returned wrong. but that doesn't fully explain intermittent dimension mismatch errors unless some nodes serve v2 variant.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): exactly. the sampler currently uses a per-shard local buffer. if shards have heterogeneous variant availability, the cross-variant path can merge when the local buffer waits and then pulls additional requests from another shard via the sampler. result: batch contains mixed-model requests; runtime assumes kernel compatibility and will execute the faster path (v2) and return 1536. client expecting 1024 sees mismatch.
Marta (Support): that aligns with customer's timeline of 'after a deploy'.
Devon (SRE): I also see a deploy-bot event at 13:01:50 for "embed-model-promotion" to embed-pool nodes.
deploy-bot: deployed embed-pool:embed-promotion v2 -> 13:01:50 UTC :white_check_mark:
Eli R (Eng Runtime): ok here's a short repro we used locally:```
# two client threads sending to same route, one expecting 1024, one default
import requests, threading
def call(expect):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'rwd-embed-large','input':['x']})
    print(expect, r.status_code, r.text)
# run many parallel to trigger coalescing
```
Eli R (Eng Runtime): in our cluster with cross_variant_coalesce=true and a mixed pool, we reproduced both the dimension mismatch and increased p95 tail.
Marta (Support): customer asks if there's a quick mitigation while you dig deeper.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): quick mitigations:
- set cross_variant_coalesce: false for the pool (will stop mixing)
- temporarily set max_batch_size to 32 to reduce cross-shard pulls
- pin the customer to a specific variant_name that guarantees dims
Any of these should reduce mismatches; the config flip can be done without code rollbacks.
Devon (SRE): I'm going to flip cross_variant_coalesce to false on embeddings-east-1 for a canary subset (one shard) and monitor.
Devon (SRE): PATCH applied to shard-2: cross_variant_coalesce=false (canary) at 13:21:08
Marta (Support): Ingrid, we'll try the canary. can you confirm if you still see the error in the next 10-15 minutes?
Ingrid (Customer): ok I'll watch.
Devon (SRE): metrics update after canary: batch_size.hist shows the canary shard cap adhered to 64, overall cluster p95 dropped ~45ms where canary traffic routed.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): thanks. I'll prepare a safer default: disable cross-variant coalescing for embedding pools unless dims match exactly in the model registry metadata. also add a sampler-level guard to reject coalescing when signature mismatch is detected.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): followups I'll own: (1) add model-dim metadata check in coalescer (2) add an alert if cross_variant_coalesce=true and model schema mismatch detected (3) postmortem with deploy gating to avoid mixed-variant live promotions.
Marta (Support): tagged SUP-6712 with those engineering followups.
support-bot: SUP-6712 updated: status=investigating, assignee=Eli R (Eng Runtime)
Ingrid (Customer): thanks all. initial mitigation seems to have reduced errors. I'll report back if anything pops. :thumbsup:
Marta (Support): closing loop: immediate mitigation = canary flip, recommended customer action = pin variant or wait for config change; engineering action = change coalescer logic + alert. assigning to Eng Runtime and SRE for postmortem and long-term fix.
Eli R (Eng Runtime): one more note - adding a small change in the scheduler to favor strict batching by variant will slightly increase cost but make behavior deterministic. will document tradeoffs.
Marta (Support): thanks team. I'll update the ticket and the customer with next steps.
Devon (SRE): leaving monitoring on for the next 48h and will escalate if tail picks back up.
Marta (Support): thanks :raised_hands:
